summary: A parse_spec function that reads a schedule written as text, such as "every 10 minutes" or "every monday at 09:00", so jobs can be configured from a settings file.
behaviour: `schedule.parse_spec(text)` reads `every <unit>`, `every <n> <units>`, `every <n> to <m> <units>` or `every <weekday>`, each optionally followed by `at <time>`. Words are separated by whitespace and may be in any case. A unit is singular (`second`, `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`) without a number and plural with one; a weekday takes no number.

It returns a dict with the keys `interval` (the number, 1 if none), `latest` (`m`, or None), `unit` (the plural unit, `weeks` for a weekday), `at` (the time as written, or None) and `start_day` (the weekday's full lowercase name, or None). A weekday is accepted in every form `Job.on()` accepts on main.
`n` and `m` are positive integers, and `m` must not be smaller than `n`.
An `at` time is accepted exactly where `Job.at()` accepts it for the same job, in the same formats: never for seconds or for plain weeks.
history: - Fixed: Jobs scheduled with until() and a time zone are cancelled on time.
